- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.67) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.33) or shows strong bearish signals.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.0) — model tends to overreact and peak too high.
- Exhibit mean reversion bias: model often fails to correct from recent highs/lows; true price tends to revert toward 70–74 range after sustained extremes.
- Lag in correction: model delays downward adjustments after negative sentiment or price drops, often missing early reversals.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts overestimate in early periods (e.g., 2025-06-10–16) when sentiment is mixed or volatile — model assumes continuation of trend rather than mean reversion.
- Avoid extrapolating sentiment trends beyond 3–5 days — sentiment decay often underestimates price correction.
